passages.text: TERMS USED BY CSX When used in this report, unless otherwise indicated by the context, these terms are used to mean the following: Car hire - A charge paid by one railroad for its use of cars belonging to another railroad or car owner. Class I freight railroad - One of the largest line haul freight railroads as determined based on operating revenue; the exact revenue required to be in each class is periodically adjusted for inflation by the Surface Transportation Board. Smaller railroads are classified as Class II or Class III. Common carrier mandate - A federal mandate that requires U.S. railroads to accommodate reasonable requests from shippers to carry any freight, including hazardous materials. Demurrage - A charge assessed by railroads for the use of rail cars by shippers or receivers of freight beyond a specified free time. Department of Transportation ("DOT") - A U.S. government agency with jurisdiction over matters of all modes of transportation. Depreciation study - Conducted by a third-party specialist and analyzed by management, a periodic statistical analysis of fixed asset service lives, salvage values, accumulated depreciation, and other factors for group assets along with a comparison of similar asset groups at other companies. Double-stack - Stacking containers two-high on specially equipped cars. Economic Profit (CSX Cash Earnings or CCE) - A non-GAAP measure designed to incentivize strategic investments earning more than the required return. Economic Profit is calculated as CSX’s gross cash earnings (after-tax adjusted EBITDA) minus the capital charge (long-term average cost of capital) on gross operating assets. Environmental Protection Agency (“EPA”) - A U.S. government agency that has regulatory authority with respect to environmental law. Federal Railroad Administration ("FRA") - The branch of the DOT that is responsible for developing and enforcing railroad safety regulations, including safety standards for rail infrastructure and equipment. Free cash flow ("FCF") - The calculation of a non-GAAP measure by using net cash provided by operating activities and adjusting for property additions and certain other investing activities. Free cash flow is a measure of cash available for paying dividends, share repurchases and principal reduction on outstanding debt. Group-life depreciation - A type of depreciation in which assets with similar useful lives and characteristics are aggregated into groups. Instead of calculating depreciation for individual assets, depreciation is calculated as a whole for each group. Incidental charges - Charges for switching, demurrage, storage, etc. Intermodal - A flexible way of transporting freight over highway, rail and water without being removed from the original transportation equipment, namely a container or trailer. CSX 2025 Form 10-K p.26 CSX CORPORATION PART II Mainline - The main track thoroughfare, exclusive of terminals, yards, sidings and turnouts. Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (“PHMSA”) - An agency within the DOT that, together with the FRA, has broad jurisdiction over railroad operating standards and practices, including hazardous materials requirements. passages.heading: Debt note
passages.text: continued Credit Facilities The Company has a $ 1.2 billion unsecured, revolving credit facility backed by a diverse syndicate of banks. This facility allows same-day borrowings at floating interest rates, based on SOFR or an agreed-upon replacement reference rate, plus a spread that depends upon CSX's senior unsecured debt ratings. This facility expires in February 2028. As of December 31, 2025, the Company had no outstanding balances under this facility. Commitment fees and interest rates payable under the facility were similar to fees and rates available to comparably rated investment-grade borrowers. As of December 31, 2025, CSX was in compliance with all covenant requirements under the facility. Commercial Paper Under its commercial paper program, which is backed by the revolving credit facility, the Company may issue unsecured commercial paper notes up to a maximum aggregate principal amount of $ 1.0 billion. Proceeds from issuances of the notes are expected to be used for general corporate purposes. At December 31, 2025, the Company had no commercial paper outstanding. CSX 2025 Form 10-K p.97 CSX CORPORATION PART II Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data NOTE 11. The Company’s performance obligation arises when it receives a bill of lading (“BOL”) to transport a customer's commodities at a negotiated price contained in a transportation services agreement or a publicly disclosed tariff rate. Once a BOL is received, a contract is formed whereby the parties are committed to perform, collectability of consideration is probable and the rights of the parties, shipping terms and conditions, and payment terms are identified. A customer may submit several BOLs for transportation services at various times throughout a service agreement term, but each shipment represents a distinct service that is a separately identified performance obligation. credit_strengths.text: Operating margin is roughly double the sector median, reflecting the efficiency of CSX's Class I line-haul rail network and pricing power across merchandise, intermodal and coal franchises. This structural cost advantage underpins cash generation even as revenue and operating income declined across the trend period.

Operating cash flow covers capital spending plus dividends with modest headroom, and covers distributions to shareholders including buybacks comfortably. Internal cash generation therefore funds the bulk of the reinvestment and shareholder return programme without reliance on incremental borrowing.

key_risks.text: Gross and net leverage sit above the sector median and rose year on year, with net leverage just below the next risk-band boundary. A modest EBITDA decline or incremental debt would push the indicative profile lower, leaving limited cushion at the current tier.

Disclosed risks include trade tariffs and international trade agreements affecting freight demand, competition from trucking, severe weather and hazardous-materials or cybersecurity incidents. Coal revenue already fell sharply year on year, illustrating how volume and commodity exposure can erode earnings and cash flow quickly.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage remains solid in absolute terms but declined year on year and trails the sector median, while EBITDA coverage similarly softened. Debt service is comfortably met from operating income, yet the downward trajectory warrants monitoring as interest expense absorbs a rising share of earnings.

Free cash flow to debt fell year on year and is well below the sector median, and free cash flow does not cover dividends plus buybacks, so distributions are partly funded from other sources. Liquidity is thin, with a current ratio below one and below peers, though undrawn committed facilities provide backup.

overall_credit_view.text: CSX retains a strong franchise and superior margins, but leverage above the sector median, weakening coverage and free cash flow that trails distributions point to a deteriorating trajectory. The indicative financial risk profile is Significant, and the narrow headroom to the next leverage boundary makes deleveraging or sustained EBITDA recovery the key credit driver.

Refinancing risk appears contained: the revolving facility runs to a medium-term maturity and was undrawn at year end, with no commercial paper outstanding and covenant compliance affirmed. Our forward view is that liquidity and maturity coverage remain adequate, but shareholder returns absorbing free cash flow limit the pace of debt reduction.

credit_strengths.text: 營運利潤率約為行業中位數的兩倍，反映CSX一級幹線鐵路網絡的效率，以及在雜貨、聯運和煤炭業務上的定價能力。此結構性成本優勢支撐現金生成，即使收入及營運收入於趨勢期內下降。
營運現金流覆蓋資本開支加股息後仍有溫和餘裕，並能舒適地覆蓋包括回購在內的股東分派。因此，內部現金生成可為大部分再投資及股東回報計劃提供資金，而無需依賴新增借貸。

key_risks.text: 總槓桿及淨槓桿高於行業中位數並按年上升，淨槓桿僅略低於下一個風險區間邊界。EBITDA溫和下降或新增債務將推低指示性狀況，令目前級別下的緩衝有限。
披露風險包括影響貨運需求的貿易關稅及國際貿易協議、來自貨車運輸的競爭、惡劣天氣，以及危險品或網絡安全事件。煤炭收入已按年大幅下降，說明貨量及商品敞口可迅速侵蝕盈利及現金流。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋在絕對值上仍然穩健，但按年下降並落後於行業中位數，而EBITDA覆蓋亦同樣轉弱。債務償付可從營運收入中舒適地滿足，但隨着利息開支佔盈利比重上升，其下行軌跡值得監察。
自由現金流對債務比率按年下降，並遠低於行業中位數，且自由現金流不足以覆蓋股息加回購，因此分派部分由其他來源提供資金。流動性偏薄，流動比率低於一且低於同業，儘管未提取的承諾融資提供備用支持。

overall_credit_view.text: CSX保留強大業務基礎及優越利潤率，但槓桿高於行業中位數、覆蓋轉弱，以及自由現金流落後於分派，均指向惡化軌跡。指示性財務風險狀況為Significant，而距離下一個槓桿邊界的緩衝狹窄，使去槓桿或持續EBITDA復甦成為關鍵信用驅動因素。
再融資風險似乎受控：循環融資額度至中期到期，並於年末未提取，且無未償還商業票據，並確認遵守契約。我們的前瞻觀點是流動性及到期覆蓋仍然充足，但股東回報吸收自由現金流限制了減債步伐。
